families.text: Inter (variable, self-hosted on web; system-ui on iOS and Android)
families.display: Fraunces (variable, self-hosted; headlines and figures only)

typography.minimumRenderedNote: The floor tests/accessibility.spec.ts enforces on rendered text, and it is the caption size above rather than minimumBody. That is a gap, said out loud: this design puts unread counts, chart axes and tab-bar labels at the caption size, and the caption size is two points under what the same file calls the minimum for body text. Raising the caption to 13 is a type-scale decision with a layout consequence on every dense screen, so it is proposed rather than taken here. What was closed is the drift below the scale — a 9px count and a 10px tab label were not decisions, they were numbers nudged to make a row fit.

targets.why: A control smaller than a fingertip is not a smaller control, it is a control somebody misses while standing in a doorway holding a child. WCAG 2.2 puts the AA floor at 24x24 (SC 2.5.8) and the AAA figure at 44x44 (SC 2.5.5); this design is held to 44 because it is a health app operated one-handed, and everything that is not is listed below with what it measures instead. tests/accessibility.spec.ts reads this list, so an exemption is a line in the contract rather than a line in a test.
targets.exemptions: A link inside a running paragraph, and an input the design hides behind its own label — the label is the target and is measured in its place.

knownUndersized.note: Twenty-four square, the AA floor, and every slide it selects is also reachable from the pause control and by letting the carousel run. Making it 44 would space three dots across 132px and turn a quiet indicator into the loudest thing on the banner.

An inline text action inside a dense row — a provenance note, a call roster line. At 44 it would double the height of every row it sits in. Every one of them has a full-size equivalent elsewhere on the screen.
Only undersized where it is not a button. Where it is one — the profile control in the top bar — it is 44.

contrast.why: A palette is either measured or it is a matter of opinion, and colour is the one part of a design where an opinion held by somebody with ordinary eyesight is worth nothing to the reader who cannot use the result. Every foreground and background this design actually puts together is listed below with the ratio it has to clear, and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs computes each one from the hexes above on every build. A pair that is not listed is a pair nobody has checked, which is why adding a colour combination to the design means adding a row here first.
contrast.standard: WCAG 2.2 AA. 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text (18.66px bold or 24px and over) and for the visual boundary of a control or a focus indicator (SC 1.4.11).

knownFailures.use: Captions, helper text and metadata on a card
knownFailures.note: The largest of these and the one worth fixing first: 77 rules in styles.css set text to --faint, and at 2.95:1 it does not clear the boundary for a control, let alone for text. Darkening the token to #5F706A takes it to 5.23:1 on a card and 4.89:1 on the page ground while keeping it distinct from --body. It is not changed here because the palette belongs to whoever drew it, and a brand colour altered by an engineer in passing is how a design system stops being one.

knownFailures.use: Captions and helper text on the page ground
knownFailures.note: The same token, on the ground it appears against most often. 2.75:1 today; 4.89:1 with the proposal above.

knownFailures.use: The label of a warning pill
knownFailures.note: 3.29:1. A warning that is harder to read than the thing it is warning about. #8A5E12 gives 5.04:1 on the pill and 5.69:1 on a card — but note that --amber is also the proposed focus ring below, where anything darker still passes, so the two uses do not pull against each other.

knownFailures.use: The label of a refusal pill
knownFailures.note: 4.24:1 — under by a quarter of a point, which is exactly the kind of miss an eye does not catch. #A6392E gives 5.67:1 on the pill and 6.47:1 on a card.

knownFailures.use: Action text inside a tinted panel
knownFailures.note: 4.43:1. Not a palette problem: --teal-deep is already in the palette at 6.21:1 on this ground and is what the tinted panels should be using. The fix is a stylesheet edit rather than a new colour.

knownFailures.use: Action text inside a mint tile
knownFailures.note: 4.07:1, and the same fix: --teal-deep gives 5.70:1 here.

notMeasured.why: A decorative separator between two blocks of content. SC 1.4.11 covers the visual boundary of a control, not a rule drawn between paragraphs, and every control in this design is bounded by its own fill or by the focus ring rather than by --line.

Kept for the accent on dark panels, where it measures 5.91:1, and for a 7px unread dot that carries no information a word does not also carry beside it. It was the focus ring until this table was computed: at 2.12:1 on a card it failed SC 1.4.11, which is a keyboard-accessibility defect rather than a cosmetic one, so the ring moved to --amber and is measured above.
